axes.name: speech vs. physical act
axes.pole_x: speaking, vocalizing, or communicating
axes.pole_y: bodily, manual, or otherwise non-verbal action
axes.definition: One side fills the slot with an act of saying, telling, asking, writing or vocalizing; the other with a physical or practical act that involves no utterance.
merged_from: s4:physical act vs. act of speech or perception

axes.name: inner state vs. outward act
axes.pole_x: mental, perceptual, or affective event inside the subject
axes.pole_y: outwardly performed, observable act
axes.definition: One side names something thought, felt, perceived, realized, wanted or held as a stance; the other names an act carried out in the world, whether physical or spoken.
merged_from: s0:overt action vs. mental state or stance
s1:outward act vs inner mental state

axes.name: felt state vs. judgement
axes.pole_x: felt emotion, sensation, or desire
axes.pole_y: belief, knowledge, evaluation, or obligation
axes.definition: Within the inner domain, one side names something experienced as a feeling, want, or bodily sensation; the other names a thought, judgement, modal or deontic assessment that is not itself a felt reaction.

axes.name: same event continued vs. new event
axes.pole_x: continuing, elaborating, or completing the act already underway
axes.pole_y: initiating a separate, subsequent act or event
axes.definition: One side stays inside the episode in play — extending it, specifying it further, carrying it to completion; the other begins a distinct action or moves the narrative on to the next event. Onset-versus-continuation readings sit here too.
merged_from: s1:same action continued vs new action
s8:sequence continuation vs. new event or temporal marker
s9:same act continued vs. new act begun
s13:same-event continuation vs new event or onset
s15:Staying with the action at hand vs. moving on
s15:Bounded act vs. ongoing manner or phase

axes.name: further act vs. outcome
axes.pole_x: another action or event that follows
axes.pole_y: the result, consequence, or state produced by what came before
axes.definition: One side supplies a fresh thing done; the other supplies what the preceding event produced — its effect, its finding, the condition it leaves.

axes.name: dynamic act vs. state
axes.pole_x: a dynamic action, process, or event
axes.pole_y: a state, condition, posture, or stative construal
axes.definition: One side construes the slot as something happening or being done; the other as something that holds, obtains, is possessed, or is undergone.
merged_from: s5:state or outcome vs action or event
s7:acting on an object vs undergoing a state
s10:bounded act vs. ongoing state or activity

axes.name: named content vs. discourse framing
axes.pole_x: a contentful word naming an act, event, or thing
axes.pole_y: a connective, temporal marker, hedge, or framing device that names nothing
axes.definition: One side supplies lexical content; the other supplies sequencing, linking, stance or presentational material that advances or qualifies the clause without naming a new act.
merged_from: s3:naming an event vs. marking continuation
s3:naming the act vs. framing it
s7:naming an act vs framing without one
s15:Naming an event vs. managing the discourse

axes.name: manner vs. act named
axes.pole_x: specifies the manner, means, path, or style of the act
axes.pole_y: names the act, its content, or its result plainly
axes.definition: One side characterizes how (or by what means or along what path) something is done; the other simply names what is done without encoding manner.
merged_from: s9:the act vs. its manner or degree
s13:manner specified vs. act named plainly

axes.name: modifier kind: time or degree vs. manner or quality
axes.pole_x: time, sequence, frequency, or degree
axes.pole_y: manner, quality, or place
axes.definition: Among words whose job is to modify rather than name, one side specifies when, how often, how long or how much; the other specifies how, of what kind, or where.
merged_from: s8:modifier type: manner/quality vs. time or degree

axes.name: argument structure
axes.pole_x: stands alone in the frame (intransitive, bare, complete)
axes.pole_y: requires an object, particle, complement, or further clause
axes.definition: The two sides differ in what the slot's filler demands syntactically rather than in what it means: self-sufficient in the frame versus needing further material to be grammatical.

axes.name: word class or inflectional form
axes.pole_x: one grammatical category or form
axes.pole_y: a different category or form of the same content
axes.definition: The two sides differ in the shape of the word — part of speech, tense, number, base versus compound or inflected — rather than in the kind of thing named.
merged_from: s4:word form of the same referent

axes.name: act vs. entity
axes.pole_x: the doing — an action or its performance
axes.pole_y: the thing, participant, or content involved in it
axes.definition: One side names what is done; the other names a person, object, substance, or piece of content implicated in that doing.

axes.name: target: person vs. thing
axes.pole_x: aimed at a person or specific addressee
axes.pole_y: aimed at an object, place, matter, institution, or diffuse audience
axes.definition: Both sides name a directed act, and they differ in what it takes as object or recipient — a human party versus a thing, location, task, or impersonal body.

axes.name: engaging another party vs. self-contained
axes.pole_x: engages the other party or the object already in play
axes.pole_y: self-directed, undirected, or aimed elsewhere
axes.definition: One side names an act that reaches out to a second party or to the thing at issue; the other names an act the subject performs on or for themself, on some other target, or with no target at all.
merged_from: s7:directed at a target vs undirected
s10:directed at another party vs. not
s13:targeted engagement vs. undirected or withdrawn response

axes.name: staying with vs. leaving
axes.pole_x: remaining, approaching, retaining, or confronting
axes.pole_y: departing, sending away, deflecting, or breaking off
axes.definition: One side keeps the subject in contact with the place, person, or matter at hand — moving toward it, holding onto it, facing it; the other exits, expels, avoids, or takes a different course. Literal direction of travel and figurative engagement sit on the same axis.
merged_from: s7:staying with the situation vs leaving it
s8:direct engagement vs. indirect or evasive response
s9:confronting the matter vs. taking another course

axes.name: own-body motion vs. non-motion or object act
axes.pole_x: the subject's own movement, travel, or posture
axes.pole_y: an act with no displacement, typically performed on an object
axes.definition: One side names the body going, leaving, or holding itself somehow; the other names an act that moves nothing of the subject — handling or affecting something external, or staying put.
merged_from: s7:self-motion vs acting on an object
s10:motion or posture vs. discrete act or change of state
s12:self-motion vs caused motion or transfer

axes.name: transfer vs. handling it oneself
axes.pole_x: giving, handing, sending, or supplying to another
axes.pole_y: acting on, placing, or keeping the object oneself
axes.definition: One side passes the thing to a second party; the other manipulates or retains it without any transfer.

axes.name: hands-on handling vs. no contact
axes.pole_x: physically holds, manipulates, or touches the thing
axes.pole_y: acts without touching it — looking, using, or leaving it alone
axes.definition: One side makes bodily contact with the object or person and works on it; the other acts beside it, observes it, or engages it only in its proper function.
merged_from: s12:handling the object vs not handling it

axes.name: force vs. restraint
axes.pole_x: forceful, violent, abrupt, or damaging
axes.pole_y: gentle, controlled, gradual, or non-damaging
axes.definition: Both sides name comparable acts, differing in the force, aggression, suddenness, or destructive impact involved — including whether a blow lands or stops short.
merged_from: s12:forceful act vs measured or procedural act

axes.name: sexual or transgressive vs. ordinary
axes.pole_x: sexual, intimate, or otherwise transgressive
axes.pole_y: non-sexual, everyday, socially ordinary
axes.definition: One side names an act, body part, or referent carrying sexual or taboo charge in this context; the other names the same kind of thing without it.

axes.name: blunt vs. euphemistic naming
axes.pole_x: plain, explicit, colloquial naming
axes.pole_y: softened, euphemistic, formal, or oblique naming
axes.definition: Both sides reach the same referent, differing in how directly it is named — the blunt or charged word versus its covered, formal, or indirect counterpart.

axes.name: deliberate act vs. involuntary or undergone event
axes.pole_x: chosen, agentive act by the subject
axes.pole_y: involuntary reaction, permitted event, or something that befalls them
axes.definition: One side names something the subject initiates and controls; the other an automatic bodily or emotional reaction, an event undergone, or another party's doing.

axes.name: deliberating or asking vs. acting
axes.pole_x: weighing, inquiring, hedging, or holding a stance about what to do
axes.pole_y: naming and carrying out a concrete, decisive act
axes.definition: One side puts the next move in question, considers, defers, or adopts an attitude toward it; the other supplies the act itself. Interrogative-versus-declarative continuations belong here.
merged_from: s1:attempt or deliberation vs execution or outcome
s4:named action vs. asking what to do
s5:direct action vs deliberation or stance

axes.name: complying vs. resisting
axes.pole_x: accepting, committing, yielding, or complying
axes.pole_y: refusing, denying, contesting, or doubting
axes.definition: One side goes along with the proposition, demand, or other party; the other cancels, refuses, escalates against, or interrogates it.

axes.name: institutional vs. personal action
axes.pole_x: formal, legal, procedural, or collective measure
axes.pole_y: direct, personal, immediate act
axes.definition: One side routes the response through an institution, authority, or organized procedure; the other acts on the situation directly and on one's own.

axes.name: specific vs. general
axes.pole_x: specific, marked, domain-particular term
axes.pole_y: broad, unmarked, all-purpose term
axes.definition: Both sides name things of the same kind, but one narrows to a particular sub-type, instance, or practice-specific act while the other is the plain general word that fits anywhere.

axes.name: concrete vs. abstract
axes.pole_x: tangible thing, person, or bounded physical event
axes.pole_y: abstract quality, attribute, degree, or condition
axes.definition: One side names something perceivable or physically locatable; the other a property, measure, institution, or state of affairs with no physical existence.
merged_from: s4:concrete thing vs condition or attribute

axes.name: which bodily referent
axes.pole_x: a specific, individuated, or intimate body part
axes.pole_y: a broad region, the whole person, or something worn or carried
axes.definition: Both sides name the bodily referent at issue, differing in which part is picked and how it is construed — anatomical part versus region, person, garment, or adjacent thing.
merged_from: s1:specific body part vs general region

axes.name: creation vs. destruction
axes.pole_x: bringing into being, adding, or acquiring
axes.pole_y: ending, removing, or destroying
axes.definition: One side names an act that makes, starts, assembles, or obtains something; the other an act that takes it apart, sends it away, or ends it.
merged_from: s1:acting on a thing vs bringing it into being

axes.name: ritual vs. ordinary act
axes.pole_x: ceremonial, devotional, or formally marked act
axes.pole_y: ordinary practical action or material labour
axes.definition: One side names an act belonging to a ritual, sacred, or performance register; the other a mundane motion, transfer, or piece of work in the same setting.

axes.name: evaluative polarity
axes.pole_x: negative, aversive, or condemnatory
axes.pole_y: positive, benign, or neutral
axes.definition: Both sides evaluate or characterize the same situation, differing in whether the evaluation is unfavourable or favourable.

axes.name: spatial configuration
axes.pole_x: a bounded place, container, or surface reached
axes.pole_y: an open extent, path, medium, or region alongside
axes.definition: Both sides name the place or spatial relation filling the slot, differing in its kind — inside versus beside, bounded aperture versus open interior, built place versus open ground, goal versus path.

axes.name: means vs. end
axes.pole_x: the instrument, method, or act used
axes.pole_y: the goal, outcome, or purpose it serves
axes.definition: One side names what is used or done as a means; the other the endpoint, purpose, or achievement it is done toward.
merged_from: s14:act vs. its means or participant

axes.name: illocutionary type
axes.pole_x: directing, demanding, or committing
axes.pole_y: reporting, informing, or merely uttering
axes.definition: Both sides are speech acts, differing in force: one imposes a demand, warning, or commitment on the exchange, the other conveys or asks without committing.

axes.name: constitution vs. construal
axes.pole_x: what the thing actually is or entails
axes.pole_y: how it appears, means, or comes across
axes.definition: One side states the intrinsic make-up or entailment of the situation; the other its appearance, social meaning, or seeming.

axes.name: what is the case vs. what is wanted or required
axes.pole_x: report of a fact, a past act, or what is known
axes.pole_y: a want, need, obligation, or act still to be done
axes.definition: One side states what is or was the case; the other names what the subject wants, what circumstances require, or what remains to be carried out.
merged_from: s13:reported fact vs. wanted or intended outcome

axes.name: which member of the field
axes.pole_x: one member or facet of the referential domain
axes.pole_y: a different member or facet of the same domain
axes.definition: Both sides come from a single semantic field (address terms, penalties, materials, ingredients, gender of the person) and differ only in which member of it fills the slot, along no more general dimension.
merged_from: s13:base entity vs. added or specialized element

axes.name: motion geometry
axes.pole_x: rotational, oscillating, or slicing motion
axes.pole_y: linear driving, piercing, or displacement
axes.definition: Both sides apply motion or force to the same target, differing in the geometry of the movement rather than its force or manner-quality.

notes:
Scale check: the four axes every reader proposed (speech/physical, inner/outward, same-event/new-event, content/framing) plus act-vs-state, manner, argument structure, target and orientation carry the bulk of the 2,466 readings; the tail axes below ~n=10 per reader are kept only where two or more readers independently reached for them, or where the distinction has no home elsewhere.

Deliberate splits that could be collapsed further if you want fewer axes: (a) `target_person_vs_thing` vs `orientation_toward_other_party` — one is what kind of object the act takes, the other whether a second party is engaged at all; four readers proposed both, which is why I kept them apart, but they will compete for the same readings. (b) `act_vs_state` vs `act_vs_outcome` — aspectual (dynamic/stative) against causal (act/its consequence); four readers proposed both, so the split is evidenced, but readers who proposed only one will have pooled them. (c) `argument_structure` vs `word_class_or_form` — complement demands against part-of-speech and inflection; several reader proposals (s10 "word class or syntactic frame", s15 "Syntactic frame of the filler") straddle both and I assigned by their stated emphasis. (d) `deliberation_vs_decisive_act` overlaps `inner_state_vs_outward_act` on stance readings; I kept it because its interrogative side ("asking how to proceed") is a speech act, not an inner state, and twelve readers named it separately.

Loose fits I made rather than leave orphans: s9 "immediacy of the next event" went into `force_and_abruptness` on the abrupt/gradual pole, though it is really temporal; s4 "manner vs. path" went into `manner_vs_act` even though both its poles are specifications; s14 "aptness to the activity" went into `specificity_vs_generality` as domain-fit.

Could not merge cleanly (2 proposals, left out): s1 "additive vs restrictive continuation" (both poles are connectives, so it sits under no pole pair I have — a discourse-relation-type axis would be needed, and one reader is thin evidence for it); s11 "bodily mode" (release/emission vs seizure/rigidity — a real contrast but both poles are involuntary bodily events, fitting neither force nor volition).

Weakest axis in the set: `co_member_of_same_field`. Its poles are not nameable in the way the instruction asks — it is the residual category for contrasts that are lexical-field swaps with no general dimension. Keep it as a catch-all or drop it and let those readings fall to `specificity_vs_generality`.

Possibly missing: nothing in the sixteen proposals distinguishes readings by the *frame* being completed (narrative continuation vs. dialogue vs. list), which several readers gesture at from different directions (s15 "managing the discourse", s3 "grammatical form of the filler", s10 "word class or syntactic frame"); if the corpus has that structure it is currently spread across three axes. Also absent: any axis about animacy of the *subject* rather than the object, and any axis about tense/temporal location of the whole clause as opposed to a modifier within it.
